facts.text: Bath was granted in 1761 by Governor Benning Wentworth and named after William Pulteney, 1st Earl of Bath.
The town sits at the head of navigation on the Connecticut River, shielded by the Green and White Mountains, making it a historic trade hub.
The White Mountains Railroad opened in 1853, shipping Bath's lumber, potatoes, livestock, and wood pulp to distant markets.
The Brick Store, built in 1824 by Alexander Parris, dominated the town center until its closure in 2020.
The Swiftwater Covered Bridge, the longest in New Hampshire, spans the Ammonoosuc River and nearby Big Eddy Swimming Hole is a local summer favorite.
A disastrous fire in 1872 destroyed Bath's Congregational church and Bath Hotel, but the church was rebuilt in 1873, preserving the town's historic character.
